items.title: The Impact of Investor Sentiment on Earnings Management and Financial Disclosure Behavior: Evidence from China’s A-Share Market
Deep Sentiment, Deeper Insights: LSTM and GRU Models for Reliance Stock Price Forecasting
items.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
items.summary: In this research, the impact of financial news sentiment on enhancing stock price forecasting is analyzed by incorporating sentiment features with market historical data and applying deep learning models.
items.finding: The findings show that sentiment-augmented models consistently outperform price only models on a variety of performance measures such as forecasting accuracy and directionality prediction.

items.title: The Triadic Law of Infrastructure Resilience: De-Risking Capital Allocation via the Three-Point Architecture Principle
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary: Large-scale infrastructure investments routinely suffer from severe stranded asset risk and mispriced capital due to fragmented, highly customized, project-by-project engineering designs.
items.finding: Ultimately, this framework shifts infrastructure due diligence from chaotic, project-level engineering reviews to a systematic, boundary-enforced protocol that unlocks embedded real options and compresses equity risk premiums for long-term institutional…

items.title: Is SpaceX Worth $1.75 Trillion or More?—A Value Investing Perspective
items.summary: In its 2026 initial public offering, SpaceX sought a market “valuation” of up to $1.75 trillion and ultimately achieved a market capitalization of approximately $1.77 trillion.
items.finding: Using SpaceX as a case study, this article develops a value investing framework for the valuation of New Space companies.

items.title: Externalities of Responsible Investments
items.summary: ABSTRACT We develop a model to study the efficiency of socially responsible investing (SRI) as a mechanism to control firms' externalities.
items.finding: In equilibrium, responsible investors continue to favor concentration even as SRI becomes more popular, and concentrate the most when concentration is least desirable.

items.title: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions
items.summary: Prior studies on cryptocurrency momentum overlook liquidation risk and other real-world frictions and inadequately assess its profitability.
items.finding: When portfolios are marked to market daily, many cross-sectional momentum portfolios are liquidated, and those with statistically significant mean returns often earn negative profits.

items.title: Business Portfolio Diversification and AI-driven Growth Strategy: Case Study of Microsoft
items.publisher: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
items.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
items.summary: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, large-scale technology firms generally face the challenge of balancing the stability of mature businesses with new growth opportunities.
items.finding: The research results show that business diversification can support Microsoft's AI-driven growth, but this higher growth potential is accompanied by more pronounced market risks.

items.title: Data-Driven Dynamic Portfolio Selection with Vine Copula Simulation and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: We develop a data-driven approach to dynamic portfolio selection that combines vine-copula simulation with reinforcement learning.
items.finding: Combining simulated and historical training data reduces monthly target-to-target turnover by 41.5% relative to training on historical data alone, while maintaining comparable growth.

items.title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
items.summary: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast?
items.finding: The experiment measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition; it establishes neither an internal reasoning mechanism nor realized return predictability.

items.title: Explaining Drawdowns: An ADCC Framework for Communicating Losses with Clarity and Trust
AI Washing and Stock Returns: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Firms
items.publisher: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
items.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
items.summary: Artificial intelligence has become increasingly prominent in corporate disclosure, yet firms' AI-related narratives may not always be supported by observable investment in technology or human capital.
items.finding: These results suggest that investors do not treat AI-related disclosure independently of observable corporate activity.

items.title: SOCIAL MEDIA SENTIMENT, HERDING BEHAVIOUR AND RETAIL INVESTOR ACTIVITY IN THE INDIAN STOCK MARKET: A SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Risk, Specialization, and Covered‐Interest Parity
items.summary: ABSTRACT Prevailing theories of financial intermediation assume an integrated financial sector with frictionless risk‐sharing.
items.finding: Our results highlight the importance of intermediary specialization and its impact on risk premia.

items.title: Price efficiency and equity risk premiums: A multicountry examination
Long-Term Thinking
items.summary: Why should we adhere to long-term thinking in investment?
items.finding: Because investment inherently involves sacrificing current consumption in pursuit of higher returns in the future.

items.title: Risk Measures for the Climate Transition Age: Why Symmetric Risk Budgets are unlikely to mitigate two-dimensionally asymmetric Climate Change risks
items.summary: The most widely used investment risk measures - variance, standard deviation, and tracking error - treat upside deviations as equally undesirable as downside losses.
items.finding: We propose specific changes to mandate design that would allow institutional investors to pursue climate transition opportunities within genuinely risk-aware (rather than deviation-averse) frameworks.

items.title: When Do Fundamentals Matter?
items.summary: When people describe the reason for share price moves or shifts in bond yields, it is almost always in fundamental terms.
items.finding: This investor-led price move can morph into a profound fundamental problem as these higher yields create higher debt service costs and increasing political pressure.

items.title: Lessons from the Masters: Communicating Investment Wisdom to Clients, Boards, and Regulators
ESG Integration and Risk-Adjusted Returns: Evidence from the S&P 500 (2019–2024)
items.publisher: International journal of research and scientific innovation
items.venue: International journal of research and scientific innovation
items.summary: This study investigates the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) integration and risk-adjusted returns among S&P 500 constituent firms over the period 2019–2024.
items.finding: Our findings reveal that the S&P 500 ESG Index delivered a cumulative outperformance of approximately 17.5 percentage points over the benchmark during the sample period, driven predominantly by stock selection effects rather than sector rebalancing.
